title: Release provenance correction, installed-app lifecycle verification and final acceptance readiness

baseline.note: Historical baselines. Neither is evidence for an M42.2 change; only a run whose head_sha equals the final candidate is.

innosetup_provenance_defect.observed_in: release-metadata.json and acceptance-report.json published by the M42.1 Windows gate at the baseline SHA above
innosetup_provenance_defect.published_as: build_tools.inno_setup, reported by the acceptance report as installer_compilation.inno_setup_version with status PASS
innosetup_provenance_defect.mechanism: packaging/build_windows.ps1 recorded (Get-Item ISCC.exe).VersionInfo.FileVersion; the ISCC.exe delivered by the pinned Chocolatey package carries no VS_VERSIONINFO block, so PowerShell reports 0.0.0.0
innosetup_provenance_defect.root_cause: the release tooling treated an executable resource as toolchain identity, and both generators validated only for absence (None/empty/NOT_BUILT) rather than for verifiability
innosetup_provenance_defect.reproduction: Reproduced locally against the pre-fix code: release_metadata.write_manifest(..., innosetup_version='0.0.0.0') succeeded and acceptance_report.build_report() on the resulting directory reported installer_compilation.status=PASS with inno_setup_version=0.0.0.0. After the fix the same call raises before any manifest is written, and a manifest that only claims verification is refused by the report generator

toolchain_identity_policy.authoritative_identity: installed package specification (%ProgramData%\chocolatey\lib\innosetup\innosetup.nuspec), falling back to a local package-manager query
toolchain_identity_policy.caller_supplied_value: recorded as operator-attested with innosetup_identity_verified=false; the acceptance report refuses to publish a release claim against it
toolchain_identity_policy.diagnostic_field: innosetup_compiler_file_version, which may legitimately be 0.0.0.0 or UNAVAILABLE and is never the published identity
drift_cases_that_fail: installing the pinned version while publishing 0.0.0.0 fails in release_metadata.write_manifest
publishing NOT_BUILT while an installer exists fails in release_metadata.write_manifest
claiming a verified version with no successful installed-version verification fails in acceptance_report.read_innosetup_identity
an expected version that disagrees with the recorded one fails in acceptance_report.read_innosetup_identity

manifest_schema.changed_because: the Inno Setup field's meaning changed from a raw executable resource to a verified installed-package identity, so the schema was versioned rather than silently redefined; v1 manifests are refused, not reinterpreted

artifact_verification.shared_helper: release_metadata.sha256_file streams 1 MiB blocks; acceptance_report imports it, so exactly one file-hashing implementation exists in the release tooling
artifact_verification.runner_side: the workflow additionally re-hashes with Get-FileHash, requires the v2 schema, requires innosetup_identity_verified, and requires the recorded identity to equal the version it verified
artifact_verification.environment_limitation: Actions log and artifact blob endpoints are unreachable from the working sandbox, so the manifest identity and digests are also published as a job annotation; direct third-party download re-verification remains an operator action

installed_lifecycle.step: Installed-application lifecycle smoke (silent install, run, uninstall)
isolation: work root under RUNNER_TEMP, outside the repository
bootstrap credential variables cleared before the installed executable runs
cleanup in a finally block including failure paths
installer hash verified against release metadata before execution
installed_lifecycle.proves: the published installer installs silently, the installed executable is the built version, the installed application starts and writes nothing into its own directory, and uninstall removes application files while leaving data outside {app} in place
does_not_prove: upgrade over a previous version (never simulated by running one installer twice)
retention of a real operator profile or production database
installed_lifecycle.corrected_in_m42_3: installed_smoke additionally requires the PACKAGE_SMOKE_OK success marker and rejects a FATAL or Traceback marker, so a zero exit code from the installed executable no longer satisfies the step

signing.method: Windows Get-AuthenticodeSignature per signature-bearing published file
signing.archives: recorded NOT_APPLICABLE and excluded from the aggregate; a ZIP has no Authenticode state
signing.unknown_states: an empty or unparsable status is UNKNOWN, never folded into UNSIGNED
signing.gate_effect: a signing state (including FAIL) is recorded and annotated but never fails the packaging gate; only a signing step that produced no record at all does
signing.corrected_in_m42_3: the bundle executable is examined as extracted from the hash-verified portable archive rather than as a loose copy in the release directory; a required signing record that is absent is now a report error rather than NOT_VERIFIED; and the status vocabulary is defined once in packaging/release_metadata.py and imported by every module that has to agree about what a status word means
signing.key_material_handling: no certificate, private key, PFX or password is read, printed or stored; only the names of credential-bearing environment variables are recorded, never their values
signing.prerequisite: an owner-controlled code-signing certificate or hosted signing service plus a signing step in packaging/build_windows.ps1; unsigned builds do not fail the gate because that would misattribute an external decision to repository code

internal_gates.requirement: success on the exact final SHA for Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, including exact-source, locked dependency, test and wheel verification

success on the exact final SHA for the Windows regression suite, the portable bundle, the frozen executable smoke, installer compilation with a verified Inno Setup identity, artifact hash and size re-verification, the installed-application lifecycle smoke, signature-status recording, and acceptance-report generation with the required field set

gate_result_policy: A commit cannot contain the identity of the run that validates it. Run IDs, conclusions, test counts and artifact digests are recorded in the mission report and in the runtime-generated acceptance-report.json artifact, never in committed source.

preserved_boundaries.packaging_toolchain_pins: unchanged from the M42.1 closure (pyinstaller 6.11.1, pefile 2023.2.7, altgraph 0.17.5, setuptools 84.0.0, pywin32-ctypes 0.2.3, hooks 2025.1); M42.2 changes how the installer version is verified, not what is installed
preserved_boundaries.engineering_scope: M41 boundaries retained; no standards-compliance claim is added by this checkpoint
